title: Stalemate & Draw Traps
subtitle: Don't let a won game slip into a draw.

steps.say: The cruelest moment in chess: you're up a whole queen, you make one careless move... and the game is a DRAW. Stalemate means the opponent has no legal move but is not in check. Let's make sure it never happens to you.
Watch a full queen advantage evaporate in one move.

autoMoves.say: Looks harmless... but count Black's moves: g8 and g7 are covered by the king, and now the queen's diagonal covers h7. No moves, no check — STALEMATE. Draw. Half a point thrown away.

steps.prompt: Same position — your move. One queen move mates, others draw on the spot. Find the mate!
hints: The king's only breathing square is h7. Mate must attack h8 AND cover h7 — or come from the h-file itself.
Slide the queen to the h-file: check from the front, escape squares already covered by your king.

line.say: Checkmate! The h-file check covers h7 too, and your king seals g7 and g8. One line, total control.

rejections.say: STALEMATE — the diagonal quietly seals h7, Black has nothing legal, draw. The difference between +9 and +0.5 was one square.
Check on the long diagonal — but the king ducks to h7 and the game goes on. The h-FILE was the killer, not the diagonal.

steps.wrongSay: Careful — every non-checking move that seals h7 is a draw. Find the check that covers everything.
steps.successSay: Now you see stalemate BEFORE it happens. That half-point stays yours.

steps.say: Draw trap number two: DEAD MATERIAL. Some armies simply cannot checkmate, ever: king alone, king + one bishop, king + one knight. If you're losing, trading into these is salvation; if you're winning, avoid giving your last pawns away!

steps.prompt: Black is down to a king and one stuck pawn. Mate in one — but one natural move is instant stalemate!
hints: Count Black's legal moves: the king has none, and the g7 pawn is blocked by your king. Zero moves means any quiet move from you is stalemate — you MUST give check.
Give check on the back rank — the f-file is open all the way to f8.

line.say: Checkmate! Check on the eighth, g8 covered by the queen, h7 covered by your king — and the g7 pawn can only watch.

rejections.say: STALEMATE! The king can't move, and the poor g7 pawn is frozen by your own king. Black had exactly zero moves — you had to give check. Always count the opponent's LAST legal moves in the endgame.

steps.wrongSay: Black's king AND pawn are both frozen — any non-check that keeps it that way is a draw. Check!
steps.successSay: The frozen-pawn stalemate is the most common accidental draw in beginner endgames. You're immune now.
